title: Anxious wait for mum who stormed into a classroom to confront her daughter's alleged bullies
text:
Charges could be presented against the filmed mother, confronting and threatening to damage her daughter’s classmates.
The woman broke into a classroom earlier this month and threatened to “cut” the throat of a 12 -year -old girl after the thugs allegedly told her daughter to hang.
Despite having 20 weeks pregnant, he faced his daughter’s alleged thugs in a diatribe in a bad mood in St Paul’s College in Gillies Plains, the northeastern Adelaide on February 3, a few days after classes resumed for the first time in 2025.
Ten days later, the police investigation of southern Australia on the incident is ongoing.
The mother confirmed to Seven news On Thursday, police contacted her, but added that she has not yet been formally interviewed.
Her family supports her and believes that possible positions would be deeply unfair.
They are still proud of her for confronting the alleged thugs and blame for school for not protecting the woman’s daughter.
‘When you are in your ingenuity, and you break yourself, that’s not what is going through your mind. He is protecting his children, ” a relative told Seven News.

“The University remains committed to their duty to take care of all students and staff,” he wrote.
‘We provide an environment in which the safety and well -being of all are our highest priority. We will continue to ensure the best possible support for our students and staff during this time.
“We continue to work closely with the South Australia Police and, as a result, we cannot provide more details about the incident.”
The Prime Minister of Australia del Sur, Peter Malinauskas, evaluated the controversy at that time, describing the mother’s behavior as “indefensible” and “amazing.”
“I don’t know what the circumstances that led the parents to say those things, but whatever they were, they do not approve or justify those comments under any circumstance,” he said.
“How is that behavior rationalized, how someone in their own mind justifies or rationalizes that behavior?”
